title: Version Mismatch
definition: A situation where the installed version and saved version of a software library or package differ, leading to compatibility issues.

difficulty_levels.beginner: When you save a file using one version of a software library, and then try to load it with a different version, you might encounter errors because the library's structure or features have changed.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Version mismatch refers to the discrepancy between the version of a library at the time of saving a model or configuration and the version currently installed, leading to incompatibilities.
difficulty_levels.expert: Version mismatch is a common issue in software development where the version of a library changes between saving and loading a model, causing errors due to differences in library structure, features, or functionality.

extra_fields.insight: Understanding the importance of ensuring compatibility between saved and installed versions of libraries.
